items.label: f03-two-layers
items.front: Idempotency in Atlas has two layers. What does each do?
items.back: The middleware dedupes an identical retry at the edge (same key: replay the bytes); the use case's natural-key guard makes a genuine re-entry (different key, same run) a no-op.

items.label: f01-five-flaws
items.front: Atlas flaw ledger: the five planted flaws?
items.back: 1 double on the FX fast path; 2 DateTime.Now in probation math; 3 PayInvoice guards only on status (double-pay window); 4 events published before commit; 5 GetWorker loads by id without tenant scope (IDOR).

items.label: f02-blind-spot
items.front: The reviewer skill the flaw ledger teaches?
items.back: Look at the boring neighbor of the brilliant code: in each planting PR the reviewer sincerely praised a correct pattern right next to the bug, and attention slid past it.

items.label: f04-three-history
items.front: Three "history" problems that look like one?
items.back: Effective dating (what terms apply on date X), audit trail (who changed what, when), soft delete (can we un-remove it; often a smell). Business time is DateOnly, system time DateTimeOffset UTC.

items.prompt: An annual €100,000 is rounded to 8,333.33 per month and paid twelve times. What does the year sum to?

choices.text: 100,000.00 exactly, because the rounding errors cancel out
99,999.88 in total, one cent lost in each of the 12 months
99,999.96 in total, so four cents vanish from the year
100,000.04 in total, as each month rounds up by a fraction

choices: 100,000.00 exactly, because the rounding errors cancel out
99,999.88 in total, one cent lost in each of the 12 months
99,999.96 in total, so four cents vanish from the year
100,000.04 in total, as each month rounds up by a fraction

items.explanation: 12 x 8,333.33 = 99,999.96. Largest-remainder allocation gives four months 8,333.34 and eight months 8,333.33, summing to exactly 100,000.00.

choices.text: A Roslyn analyzer rewrites each DateTime.Now call into an IClock call
Warnings-as-errors turns each DateTime.Now into a build error
Reviewers must tick a checklist item about clocks on every PR
A test scans the Atlas.Domain source files and fails on any match

Warnings-as-errors turns each DateTime.Now into a build error
Reviewers must tick a checklist item about clocks on every PR

items.explanation: AmbientTimeBanTests is a fitness function: it walks every .cs file under src/Atlas.Domain and fails on DateTime.Now/UtcNow or DateTimeOffset.Now/UtcNow, so the pattern cannot quietly return.

items.prompt: Which kind of test catches the rounding drift that only appears on salaries not divisible by twelve?

choices.text: An architecture test that bans decimal division inside the domain
A golden file showing one hand-computed worker at a round salary
A property test that sums the periods to annual for any salary
A snapshot test comparing one payslip with the previous month

choices: An architecture test that bans decimal division inside the domain
A golden file showing one hand-computed worker at a round salary
A property test that sums the periods to annual for any salary
A snapshot test comparing one payslip with the previous month

items.explanation: Golden files convince an auditor with one worked example; the property test asserts the invariant over many inputs and catches the class of bug a single example cannot.

3.33, 3.33 and 3.33, and the lost cent is logged as rounding
3.34, 3.33 and 3.33, with the spare cent on the first share

items.prompt: A client reuses an Idempotency-Key with a different request body. What does Atlas answer?

choices.text: The first 200 response replayed, and the new body ignored
A 409, because two different requests raced on one key
A fresh execution, whose 201 replaces the stored response
A 422 from IdempotencyConflictException, with its own type

choices: The first 200 response replayed, and the new body ignored
A 409, because two different requests raced on one key
A fresh execution, whose 201 replaces the stored response
A 422 from IdempotencyConflictException, with its own type

items.explanation: The request hash (method + path + body) differs from the stored one, so the middleware throws IdempotencyConflictException, which the exception handler maps to 422 with the idempotency-conflict type.

items.prompt: An authenticated client POSTs to an invoice's /pay route with no Idempotency-Key header. What is the result?

choices.text: A 401, since the key also authenticates the calling client
A 400, since the key is mandatory on money-moving routes
It runs normally, as the key is optional on every route
It is parked until a retry arrives that carries a key

choices: A 401, since the key also authenticates the calling client
A 400, since the key is mandatory on money-moving routes
It runs normally, as the key is optional on every route
It is parked until a retry arrives that carries a key

items.explanation: IsMoneyMoving matches POSTs ending in /pay or /execute; with no key there, the middleware throws RequestValidationException, mapped to 400.

items.prompt: A worker carries 12 leave days into a new leave year and the carryover cap is 5. What does LeaveAccrual do first?

choices.text: It forfeits all 12 days, as the cap applies to the new year alone
It adds the new year's accrual first, then clips the total to 5
It keeps all 12 days and caps only the new year's fresh accrual
It cuts the carried days to 5, then adds the new year's accrual

choices: It forfeits all 12 days, as the cap applies to the new year alone
It adds the new year's accrual first, then clips the total to 5
It keeps all 12 days and caps only the new year's fresh accrual
It cuts the carried days to 5, then adds the new year's accrual

items.explanation: Cap-then-accrue: at every boundary except the hire year, carried = Math.Min(carried, cap) runs before the year's accrual is added, so a fresh year always has room for its full entitlement.

items.prompt: A worker is hired on March 16. What fraction of March's monthly accrual do they earn?

choices.text: 16/31, counting the actual days from the 16th through the 31st
15/31, counting only the days that come after the hire date
15/30, as every prorated month is treated as a 30-day month
The full month, since accrual posts at the start of each month

choices: 16/31, counting the actual days from the 16th through the 31st
15/31, counting only the days that come after the hire date
15/30, as every prorated month is treated as a 30-day month
The full month, since accrual posts at the start of each month

items.explanation: HireMonthFraction: daysWorked = daysInMonth - hiredOn.Day + 1 = 31 - 16 + 1 = 16, over DateTime.DaysInMonth = 31. Only the hire month is prorated.

items.prompt: The first POST with an Idempotency-Key returned 503. The client retries with the same key and body. What happens?

choices.text: The stored 503 is replayed, with Idempotency-Replayed: true
It is refused with a 422, since that key has already been used
It waits until the first request's 30-second key lock expires
The request runs again, because only 2xx responses are stored

choices: The stored 503 is replayed, with Idempotency-Replayed: true
It is refused with a 422, since that key has already been used
It waits until the first request's 30-second key lock expires
The request runs again, because only 2xx responses are stored

items.explanation: The middleware saves the response only when StatusCode is 2xx; a 503 must stay retryable, so nothing was stored and the retry executes normally.

items.prompt: How does Atlas record a raise when the update-terms endpoint is called?

choices.text: It updates the current row in place, keeping no prior values
It inserts a new record with its own EffectiveFrom date
It overwrites the salary column and bumps a version number
It soft-deletes the old row and then inserts the new one

choices: It updates the current row in place, keeping no prior values
It inserts a new record with its own EffectiveFrom date
It overwrites the salary column and bumps a version number
It soft-deletes the old row and then inserts the new one

items.explanation: The update endpoint performs an INSERT: history cannot be lost because no UPDATE exists, and a retroactive change is an ordinary append with a past effective date.

items.prompt: Atlas computes January 31 plus three months with DateOnly.AddMonths. What date comes back?

choices.text: May 1, because three months are counted as 90 days
An exception, because April 31 is not a valid date
May 1, because a missing April 31 rolls over into the next month
April 30, because AddMonths clamps to the last day of April

choices: May 1, because three months are counted as 90 days
An exception, because April 31 is not a valid date
May 1, because a missing April 31 rolls over into the next month
April 30, because AddMonths clamps to the last day of April

items.explanation: Statutory windows are defined in months, and DateOnly.AddMonths clamps: Jan 31 + 3 months is Apr 30. "Add a month" is not "add 30 days".

items.prompt: Flaw #4: events were published right before CommitAsync, through a sink that sent each event at once. What goes wrong when that transaction rolls back?

choices.text: The commit is retried until every consumer has acknowledged it
An event has already announced a change that never happened
The event is lost, because the rollback also undoes the publish
Nothing, since the sink buffers events until the commit succeeds

choices: The commit is retried until every consumer has acknowledged it
An event has already announced a change that never happened
The event is lost, because the rollback also undoes the publish
Nothing, since the sink buffers events until the commit succeeds

items.explanation: A sink that fires immediately has already told the world; the rollback then removes the change. That is a phantom. Publishing after commit instead risks a lost event; the outbox avoids both.

items.prompt: Why does Atlas store leave dates as DateOnly and not as DateTimeOffset?

choices.text: DateTimeOffset cannot hold any date earlier than the Unix epoch
DateOnly columns sort faster in Postgres than timestamp columns do
EF Core has no way to map a DateTimeOffset to a SQL date column
A time-of-day would bring DST and timezone bugs back into leave

choices: DateTimeOffset cannot hold any date earlier than the Unix epoch
DateOnly columns sort faster in Postgres than timestamp columns do
EF Core has no way to map a DateTimeOffset to a SQL date column
A time-of-day would bring DST and timezone bugs back into leave

items.explanation: Leave is counted in calendar days; a DateTimeOffset would invent a fictional time-of-day. Business time is DateOnly, system time is DateTimeOffset UTC.
